01 / THE BRIEF

A market opportunity.
A more specific question.

Objective

Identify which outdoor product searches are gaining attention, when interest tends to rise, and how brands can use these patterns to plan their next campaign tests.

Three questions guide this report

  1. How large was the market estimated to be?
  2. Are product categories moving in the same direction?
  3. What should the brand validate before committing budget?

Scope: Indonesia. Three specific product searches, a published industry estimate, and a recent travel survey.

The findings at a glance

01Category signals have diverged. Hiking-shoe searches rose modestly, while carrier and camping-tent searches fell in the comparable 2026 period.

02Seasonality differs by product. Mid-year interest is a recurring feature; tents also show a stronger December pattern.

03The outlook is directional. Forecast errors and the limits of search data matter when translating interest into a business decision.

Market context→Consumer signals→Tested outlook→Commercial hypotheses
02 / MARKET CONTEXT

A sizeable category,
with a dated forecast.

Published market estimates establish the backdrop. They do not tell us what the market actually reached in 2025 or 2026.

2022 MARKET ESTIMATE$1.27bn

Hiking and trekking gear represented an estimated 50% of this broader market.

The definition also includes diving and swimming equipment. More specific estimates are needed to assess individual product markets.
Forecast disclaimer

The $1.69bn figure for 2025 was projected in 2023. Realized 2025 revenue has not been verified here.

Implication

Use the industry estimate to frame the opportunity. Use current category evidence to decide what to investigate.

03 / CATEGORY SIGNALS

One market.
Different directions.

The three search terms tell different stories. Compare like periods before interpreting a rise or fall.

Category momentumFigure 02

The January–October average weekly index rose 4.2% for “sepatu hiking”. Over the same comparison, “tas carrier” fell 6.9% and “tenda camping” fell 13.4%.

This is evidence of changing search interest for these exact terms. It does not establish a change in product sales, market share, or the whole category.

Implication

Validate product-specific opportunities. A broad outdoor growth story is too general to set the same priority for every category.

04 / THE SEASONAL PATTERN

Timing deserves
its own analysis.

Compare months within each year first, then average across four full years. This reduces the effect of changing annual interest levels.

MID-YEAR

June and July are worth preparing for.

All three terms show above-average interest around the middle of the year in this historical summary. Build content and test messages ahead of that window.

YEAR-END

Tents have a more distinct December lift.

The camping-tent December index is about 122, versus an annual baseline of 100. The same lift is less pronounced for the other terms.

Implication

Plan tests around each product’s pattern. Check weather, holiday shifts, stock and conversion data before setting a campaign calendar.

05 / THE CONSUMER CONTEXT

The holiday audience
is making trade-offs.

A November 2026 Jakpat survey provides timely travel context. The survey does not identify confirmed outdoor-equipment buyers.

AMONG 345 VACATION / STAYCATION PLANNERS42%

consider ticket and accommodation prices.

Travel costs are a key consideration in this subgroup. A clear, practical value proposition is a useful hypothesis to test.

This does not measure willingness to pay for outdoor gear. That needs product-specific research.

Planning window

32% of respondents usually book flights or accommodation 2–4 weeks ahead, while another 32% book more than a month ahead. This concerns travel reservations, not gear purchases.

Implication

Test messages around practical use and value. Ask buyers what they need and when they buy before inferring a gear-purchase window.

06 / THE 12-WEEK OUTLOOK

A forecast with
its limits in view.

A small set of models was compared in time order. The final 12 completed weeks were kept out of model selection.

LOCKED HOLDOUT MAE—index points · lower is better
SEASONAL BASELINE MAE—same week of the prior year
HOLDOUT WITHIN SHADED RANGE—of 12 held-out observations

How was the outlook tested?

Development compares last observation, a 52-week seasonal naive baseline, a 13-week mean, and regularized harmonic regression. Eleven rolling origins each predict 12 weeks; the lowest development MAE selects a method separately for each term.

The untouched holdout covers week starts 16 August–1 November 2026. Final forecasts refit on all 260 completed weeks. The week starting 8 November is excluded from training because collection took place before that week finished.

The shaded range uses the 10th and 90th percentiles of pooled development errors. Windows overlap, and the range is not calibrated for an 80% probability. Its observed holdout coverage is reported above. Forecasts can miss shocks or changing search behavior.

Implication

Use the outlook to time a small demand test. Inventory and revenue decisions need sales, margins and lead-time evidence as well.

07 / IMPLICATIONS FOR BRANDS

Turn signals into
testable decisions.

These recommendations should be checked against each brand’s sales, margins, customer needs and stock availability.

01
CATEGORY PRIORITY

Validate footwear interest before expanding the range.

“Sepatu hiking” has the strongest recent direction of the three exact search terms. Check category fit and current product availability, then test a product concept or relevant content with a small audience.

Look forQualified product interest, customer needs and contribution margin.
02
CAMPAIGN TIMING

Prepare earlier for category-specific seasonal windows.

Use the mid-year pattern for a planning test. For camping-related offers, separately assess the December signal. Set timing using actual stock, local conditions and customer purchase lead times.

Look forConversion and acquisition cost versus a comparable campaign window.
03
VALUE PROPOSITION

Make practical value easy to understand.

Travel-budget considerations suggest a useful starting hypothesis: explain product use, durability and the value of an appropriate bundle. Interview buyers before changing prices or positioning.

Look forReasons to buy, willingness to pay and response to a focused message test.
Test one product category before increasing the budget.
Track conversion, acquisition cost and margin.
08 / THE EVIDENCE

Sources & methodology.

01

Outdoor market estimates

PT Sinar Eka Selaras Tbk, IPO prospectus dated 2 August 2023, printed pp. 187–189 (PDF pp. 219–221). Industry research attributed to Frost & Sullivan (2023). 2018–2022 are historical estimates; 2023–2025 are forecasts published in 2023. Realized 2025 values are not verified.

Read the prospectus
02

Google Trends · original comparison export

Retrieved 14 November 2026. Indonesia, Web Search, All categories, Past 5 years. Exact terms: “tas carrier”, “tenda camping”, “sepatu hiking”. 261 weekly rows, 14 November 2021–8 November 2026. All three terms were exported in the same comparison.

Indices are sampled, normalized search interest. They are not absolute search counts, people, purchases or market share. Search terms do not cover all synonyms. Retrievals may differ because of sampling.

Open the comparison How Google Trends works
03

Jakpat · year-end holiday survey

“Year-End Holidays: Staying at Home Is More Popular Than Traveling?”, published 10 November 2026. Overall sample: 1,180 respondents. The cost consideration uses the 345 respondents planning a vacation or staycation. Percentages are rounded. The article does not establish a representative sample of outdoor-product buyers.

Read the research article
04

Forecast evaluation principles

Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, chapter 5. Time-ordered evaluation and simple benchmark methods inform the approach; the models and calculations in this report are independent project work.

Read the forecasting reference
05

Calculations & scope

Year-to-date comparison: average weekly index for week starts in January–October; 43 points in both 2025 and 2026. Seasonality: four complete years, 2022–2025; monthly mean divided by the same year’s mean, then averaged. Weekly observations are grouped by week-start month and are not exact calendar-month search totals.

Latest incomplete week excluded from model fitting. Model selection uses development data only; the final 12 completed weeks remain a locked holdout. Full model settings and results are included in the downloadable analysis.
